answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks via MPC-TLS proofs with deterministic nullifiers. An agent runs a two-party TLS session with a notary against a telecom or bank server, then submits a zero-knowledge proof of a hashed account nullifier without leaking PII. During a gale of signups at traffic's zenith, registries reject duplicate nullifiers so hosts cannot harbor clones. Each identity costs a scarce KYC account, though SIM farms can still supply valid credentials.
